celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿يس﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَالْقُرْآنِ الْحَكِيمِ﴾ made firm by its wondrous arrangement and its marvellous meanings

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿عَلَى﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to what precedes it ﴿صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ the way of the prophets before you: oneness of God and guidance. The tawkīd (emphasis) by the oath and other means is a rebuttal of the disbelievers' saying to him, "You are not one sent"

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿تَنْزِيلُ الْعَزِيزِ﴾ in His dominion; [also read تَنْزِيلَ] ﴿الرَّحِيمِ﴾ towards His creation; the khabar (predicate) of an implied (muqaddar) mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. the Qur'an [is ...]

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿لِتُنْذِرَ﴾ with it ﴿قَوْمًا﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تَنْزِيلُ» ﴿مَا أُنْذِرَ آبَاؤُهُمْ﴾ i.e. they were not warned, in the period between prophets (al-fatra) ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ i.e. the people ﴿غَافِلُونَ﴾ of faith and right guidance

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿لَقَدْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ﴾ has become binding ﴿عَلَى أَكْثَرِهِمْ﴾ with punishment ﴿فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ i.e. the majority

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ أَغْلَالًا﴾ in that the hands are joined to them, because the shackle joins the hand to the neck ﴿فَهِيَ﴾ the hands, joined ﴿إِلَى الْأَذْقَانِ﴾ plural of dhaqan, which is where the two jawbones meet ﴿فَهُمْ مُقْمَحُونَ﴾ raising their heads, unable to lower them. This is a figurative representation (tamthīl), and what is meant is that they do not submit to faith and do not lower their heads to it

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا﴾ with the sīn vowelled with fatḥa and with ḍamma in both places ﴿فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ﴾ also a figurative representation of the blocking of the way of faith for them

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَسَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully (taḥqīq), with the second changed into an alif, with it eased (tashīl), and with and without the insertion of an alif between the eased one and the other ﴿أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا تُنْذِرُ﴾ your warning benefits ﴿مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الذِّكْرَ﴾ the Qur'an ﴿وَخَشِيَ الرَّحْمَنَ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ feared Him though he has not seen Him ﴿فَبَشِّرْهُ بِمَغْفِرَةٍ وَأَجْرٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ it is Paradise

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي الْمَوْتَى﴾ for the resurrection ﴿وَنَكْتُبُ﴾ in the Preserved Tablet ﴿مَا قَدَّمُوا﴾ in their life, of good and evil, so that they may be recompensed for it ﴿وَآثَارَهُمْ﴾ what was followed as a practice after them ﴿وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ its accusative is by a verb which is explained by ﴿أَحْصَيْنَاهُ﴾ We have recorded it precisely ﴿فِي إِمَامٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ a clear book, which is the Preserved Tablet.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَاضْرِبْ﴾ set forth ﴿لَهُمْ مَثَلًا﴾ first object ﴿أَصْحَابَ﴾ second object ﴿الْقَرْيَةِ﴾ Antioch ﴿إِذْ جَاءَهَا﴾ to the end [of the clause] is a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) of «أَصْحَابَ الْقَرْيَةِ» ﴿الْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾ i.e. the messengers of Jesus

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمُ اثْنَيْنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا﴾ to the end [of the clause] is a badal (substitute) of the first «إِذْ» ﴿فَعَزَزْنَا﴾ without and with doubling [فَعَزَّزْنَا]: We strengthened the two ﴿بِثَالِثٍ فَقَالُوا إِنَّا إِلَيْكُمْ مُرْسَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿قَالُوا مَا أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنَا وَمَا أَنْزَلَ الرَّحْمَنُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنْ﴾ [meaning] «مَا» (not) ﴿أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا تَكْذِبُونَ﴾

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿قَالُوا رَبُّنَا يَعْلَمُ﴾ functioning as an oath; and the tawkīd (emphasis) was increased by it and by the lām, beyond what preceded, because of the increased denial, in ﴿إِنَّا إِلَيْكُمْ لَمُرْسَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَمَا عَلَيْنَا إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ الْمُبِينُ﴾ the conveying made manifest by clear proofs, namely healing the one born blind, the leper and the sick, and bringing the dead to life

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿قَالُوا إِنَّا تَطَيَّرْنَا﴾ we see an evil omen ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ because the rain has been cut off from us on your account ﴿لَئِنْ﴾ a lām of oath ﴿لَمْ تَنْتَهُوا لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ﴾ with stones ﴿وَلَيَمَسَّنَّكُمْ مِنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿قَالُوا طَائِرُكُمْ﴾ your evil omen ﴿مَعَكُمْ﴾ through your disbelief ﴿أَئِنْ﴾ an interrogative hamza that has entered upon the conditional «إِنْ»; and in its hamza there is full pronunciation (taḥqīq), easing (tashīl), and the insertion of an alif between it, in both its forms, and the other ﴿ذُكِّرْتُمْ﴾ you are admonished and warned; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "you see an evil omen and disbelieve", and it is the locus of the interrogation, and what is meant by it is rebuke ﴿بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُسْرِفُونَ﴾ exceeding the limit by your idolatry

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَجَاءَ مِنْ أَقْصَى الْمَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ﴾ he is Ḥabīb the Carpenter; he had believed in the messengers, and his dwelling was at the farthest end of the town ﴿يَسْعَى﴾ running fast, when he heard that the people had belied the messengers ﴿قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اتَّبِعُوا الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿اتَّبِعُوا﴾ a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first ﴿مَنْ لَا يَسْأَلُكُمْ أَجْرًا﴾ for his message ﴿وَهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ﴾ and it was said to him, "Are you of their religion?" and he said:

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَمَا لِي لَا أَعْبُدُ الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي﴾ created me, i.e. there is nothing to prevent me from worshipping Him, while what calls for it is present; and you are likewise ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ after death, and He will recompense you for your disbelief

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿أَأَتَّخِذُ﴾ in its two hamzas there is what was stated earlier for «أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ», and it is an interrogative in the sense of negation ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ idols ﴿إِنْ يُرِدْنِ الرَّحْمَنُ بِضُرٍّ لَا تُغْنِ عَنِّي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ﴾ which you have claimed ﴿شَيْئًا وَلَا يُنْقِذُونِ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of «آلِهَةً»

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿إِنِّي إِذًا﴾ i.e. if I worshipped other than Allah ﴿لَفِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ clear

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿إِنِّي آمَنْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَاسْمَعُونِ﴾ i.e. hear my word; and they stoned him and he died

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿قِيلَ﴾ to him at his death ﴿ادْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ﴾ and it is said that he entered it alive ﴿قَالَ يَا﴾ a particle for drawing attention (tanbīh) ﴿لَيْتَ قَوْمِي يَعْلَمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي﴾ of His forgiveness ﴿وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿وَمَا﴾ negative ﴿أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى قَوْمِهِ﴾ i.e. of Ḥabīb ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ after his death ﴿مِنْ جُنْدٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾ i.e. angels, to destroy them ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا مُنْزِلِينَ﴾ angels to destroy anyone

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ [meaning] «مَا» (not) ﴿كَانَتْ﴾ their punishment ﴿إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ Gabriel shouted at them ﴿فَإِذَا هُمْ خَامِدُونَ﴾ still, dead

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ﴾ these and the like of them among those who belied the messengers and were destroyed; and it (ḥasra) is intense pain, and calling it is figurative (majāz), i.e. "this is your time, so be present" ﴿مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ adduced to explain its cause, since it comprises their mockery, which led to their destruction, from which the regret was caused

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْا﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca who said to the Prophet "You are not one sent"; and the interrogative is for affirmation (taqrīr), i.e. they know ﴿كَمْ﴾ predicative (khabariyya), in the sense of "many", governed by what follows it, suspending (muʿalliqa) what precedes it from governing; and the meaning is that We ﴿أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ many ﴿مِنَ الْقُرُونِ﴾ nations ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾ i.e. those destroyed ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. to the deniers ﴿لَا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ will they not then take a lesson from them? And «أَنَّهُمْ» etc. is a badal (substitute) of what precedes it, with regard to the meaning mentioned

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ negative, or lightened (mukhaffafa) ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ i.e. all creatures; a mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿لَمَّا﴾ with doubling, in the sense of «إِلَّا», or without doubling, in which case the lām is distinguishing (fāriqa) and «مَا» is added ﴿جَمِيعٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, i.e. gathered ﴿لَدَيْنَا﴾ with Us, at the Standing after their resurrection ﴿مُحْضَرُونَ﴾ for the reckoning; a second khabar

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَهُمْ﴾ of the resurrection; a khabar (predicate) placed first ﴿الْأَرْضُ الْمَيْتَةُ﴾ without and with doubling ﴿أَحْيَيْنَاهَا﴾ with water; [«الْأَرْضُ» is] the mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿وَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهَا حَبًّا﴾ such as wheat ﴿فَمِنْهُ يَأْكُلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا جَنَّاتٍ﴾ orchards ﴿مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ وَفَجَّرْنَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْعُيُونِ﴾ i.e. some of them

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿لِيَأْكُلُوا مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ﴾ with two fatḥas and with two ḍammas, i.e. the fruit of what was mentioned, palms and other things ﴿وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ i.e. they did not make the fruit ﴿أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾ His blessings, the Exalted, upon them

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْأَزْوَاجَ﴾ the kinds ﴿كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنْبِتُ الْأَرْضُ﴾ of grains and other things ﴿وَمِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ of males and females ﴿وَمِمَّا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ of wondrous and strange creatures

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَهُمْ﴾ of the great power ﴿اللَّيْلُ نَسْلَخُ﴾ We separate ﴿مِنْهُ النَّهَارَ فَإِذَا هُمْ مُظْلِمُونَ﴾ entering into darkness

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿وَالشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي﴾ to the end [of the clause] is part of the sign for them, or another sign; and the moon likewise ﴿لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَهَا﴾ i.e. to it; it does not go beyond it ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ its running ﴿تَقْدِيرُ الْعَزِيزِ﴾ in His dominion ﴿الْعَلِيمِ﴾ of His creation

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿وَالْقَمَرُ﴾ in the nominative and the accusative [وَالْقَمَرَ], and it is accusative by a verb which is explained by what follows it ﴿قَدَّرْنَاهُ﴾ with respect to its course ﴿مَنَازِلَ﴾ twenty-eight stations in twenty-eight nights of every month; and it is hidden for two nights if the month is thirty days, and for one night if it is twenty-nine days ﴿حَتَّى عَادَ﴾ in the last of its stations, to the eye ﴿كَالْعُرْجُونِ الْقَدِيمِ﴾ like the stalk of the date clusters when it grows old, for it becomes thin, curved and yellow

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿لَا الشَّمْسُ يَنْبَغِي﴾ is easy and possible ﴿لَهَا أَنْ تُدْرِكَ الْقَمَرَ﴾ and so meet with it at night ﴿وَلَا اللَّيْلُ سَابِقُ النَّهَارِ﴾ so it does not come before its end ﴿وَكُلٌّ﴾ its nunation is in compensation for the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct): of the sun, the moon and the stars ﴿فِي فَلَكٍ﴾ circular ﴿يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ move; they are treated as beings endowed with reason.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَهُمْ﴾ of Our power ﴿أَنَّا حَمَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾ and in one reading [ذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ], i.e. their fathers, the ancestors ﴿فِي الْفُلْكِ﴾ i.e. Noah's ship ﴿الْمَشْحُونِ﴾ filled

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿وَخَلَقْنَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مِثْلِهِ﴾ i.e. like Noah's ship, and that is the small and large ships they made in its shape, through Allah the Exalted's teaching ﴿مَا يَرْكَبُونَ﴾ in [it]

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿وَإِنْ نَشَأْ نُغْرِقْهُمْ﴾ despite the ships having been brought into being ﴿فَلَا صَرِيخَ﴾ helper ﴿لَهُمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْقَذُونَ﴾ are saved

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿إِلَّا رَحْمَةً مِنَّا وَمَتَاعًا إِلَى حِينٍ﴾ nothing saves them except Our mercy towards them and Our letting them enjoy their pleasures until the end of their terms

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّقُوا مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ of the punishment of this world, like others than you ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَكُمْ﴾ of the punishment of the Hereafter ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ﴾ they turned away

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَمَا تَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا كَانُوا عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ﴾ i.e. the poor among the Companions said ﴿لَهُمْ أَنْفِقُوا﴾ on us ﴿مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ of wealth ﴿قَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ mocking them ﴿أَنُطْعِمُ مَنْ لَوْ يَشَاءُ اللَّهُ أَطْعَمَهُ﴾ according to this belief of yours ﴿إِنْ﴾ [meaning] «مَا» (not) ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ in your saying that to us together with this belief of yours ﴿إِلَّا فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ clear; and the explicit statement of their disbelief carries great weight

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَى هَذَا الْوَعْدُ﴾ of the resurrection ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in it. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿مَا يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ i.e. they wait for ﴿إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ and it is the first blast of Isrāfīl ﴿تَأْخُذُهُمْ وَهُمْ يَخِصِّمُونَ﴾ with doubling; its original form is «يَخْتَصِمُونَ»: the vowel of the tāʾ was transferred to the khāʾ, and it was assimilated into the ṣād; i.e. while they are heedless of it, disputing, trading, eating, drinking and so on; and in one reading [يَخْصِمُونَ], on the pattern of «يَضْرِبُونَ», i.e. some of them dispute with others

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ تَوْصِيَةً﴾ i.e. to make a bequest ﴿وَلَا إِلَى أَهْلِهِمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ from their markets and occupations; rather they die in them

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿وَنُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ﴾ it is the horn, the second blast, for the resurrection; and between the two blasts there are forty years ﴿فَإِذَا هُمْ﴾ i.e. those buried ﴿مِنَ الْأَجْدَاثِ﴾ the graves ﴿إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَنْسِلُونَ﴾ come out quickly

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ i.e. the disbelievers among them ﴿يَا﴾ for drawing attention (tanbīh) ﴿وَيْلَنَا﴾ our destruction; and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that has no verb from its root ﴿مَنْ بَعَثَنَا مِنْ مَرْقَدِنَا﴾ because between the two blasts they were asleep and were not punished ﴿هَذَا﴾ the resurrection ﴿مَا﴾ i.e. that which ﴿وَعَدَ﴾ of ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ وَصَدَقَ﴾ in it ﴿الْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾ they acknowledge it when acknowledgement does not benefit them; and it is said that this is said to them

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ [meaning] «مَا» (not) ﴿كَانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً فَإِذَا هُمْ جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا﴾ with Us ﴿مُحْضَرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ لَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا وَلَا تُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا﴾ the recompense of ﴿مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ الْيَوْمَ فِي شُغْلٍ﴾ with the ghayn vowelless and with ḍamma [شُغُلٍ], away from what the people of the Fire are in, with what they delight in, such as deflowering virgins; not an occupation in which they tire, because there is no toil in Paradise ﴿فَاكِهُونَ﴾ enjoying bliss; a second khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ», the first being «فِي شُغُلٍ»

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿هُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿وَأَزْوَاجُهُمْ فِي ظِلَالٍ﴾ plural of ẓulla or of ẓill; the khabar (predicate), i.e. the sun does not strike them ﴿عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ﴾ plural of arīka, which is the couch in the curtained canopy (ḥajala), or the bedding in it ﴿مُتَّكِئُونَ﴾ a second khabar, to which «عَلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq)

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿لَهُمْ فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَلَهُمْ﴾ in it ﴿مَا يَدَّعُونَ﴾ they wish for

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿سَلَامٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿قَوْلًا﴾ i.e. by speech; its khabar (predicate) is ﴿مِنْ رَبٍّ رَحِيمٍ﴾ towards them, i.e. He says to them "Peace be upon you"; and He says:

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿وَامْتَازُوا الْيَوْمَ أَيُّهَا الْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾ i.e. separate yourselves from the believers, when they have become mixed with them

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿أَلَمْ أَعْهَدْ إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ command you ﴿يَا بَنِي آدَمَ﴾ on the tongue of My messengers ﴿أَنْ لَا تَعْبُدُوا الشَّيْطَانَ﴾ do not obey him ﴿إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ﴾ clear in enmity

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿وَأَنِ اعْبُدُونِي﴾ affirm My oneness and obey Me ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ﴾ a path ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَضَلَّ مِنْكُمْ جُبْلًا﴾ creatures; plural of jabīl, like qadīm; and in one reading with ḍamma on the bāʾ [جِبِلًا] «[Translator's note: the bracketed form as printed has kasra on the jīm and the bāʾ, which does not match the description "with ḍamma on the bāʾ" (i.e. جُبُلًا); reproduced as written]» ﴿كَثِيرًا أَفَلَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ his enmity and his leading astray, or the punishment that befell them, so that you would believe; and it will be said to them in the Hereafter:

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿اصْلَوْهَا الْيَوْمَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿الْيَوْمَ نَخْتِمُ عَلَى أَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ i.e. of the disbelievers, because of their saying {وَاللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ} ﴿وَتُكَلِّمُنَا أَيْدِيهِمْ وَتَشْهَدُ أَرْجُلُهُمْ﴾ and other [limbs] ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ so every limb speaks of what issued from it

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿وَلَوْ نَشَاءُ لَطَمَسْنَا عَلَى أَعْيُنِهِمْ﴾ We would have blinded them, effacing them ﴿فَاسْتَبَقُوا﴾ they rushed to ﴿الصِّرَاطَ﴾ the path, going as was their habit ﴿فَأَنَّى﴾ then how ﴿يُبْصِرُونَ﴾ at that time? i.e. they would not see

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿وَلَوْ نَشَاءُ لَمَسَخْنَاهُمْ﴾ into apes and swine, or stones ﴿عَلَى مَكَانَتِهِمْ﴾ and in one reading [مَكَانَاتِهِمْ], plural of makāna in the sense of makān (place), i.e. in their dwellings ﴿فَمَا اسْتَطَاعُوا مُضِيًّا وَلَا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ i.e. they would be unable to go or come

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿وَمَنْ نُعَمِّرْهُ﴾ by lengthening his term ﴿نُنْكِسْهُ﴾ and in one reading [نُنَكِّسْهُ], with doubling, from tankīs ﴿فِي الْخَلْقِ﴾ i.e. his constitution, so that after his strength and youth he becomes weak and decrepit ﴿أَفَلَا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ that the One able to do that, which is known to them, is able to resurrect, and so believe? And in one reading with tāʾ

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿وَمَا عَلَّمْنَاهُ﴾ i.e. the Prophet ﴿الشِّعْرَ﴾ a rebuttal of their saying that the Qur'an he brought is poetry ﴿وَمَا يَنْبَغِي﴾ is easy ﴿لَهُ﴾ poetry ﴿إِنْ هُوَ﴾ what he brought is not ﴿إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ﴾ an admonition ﴿وَقُرْآنٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ making manifest the rulings and other things

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ﴾ with yāʾ and tāʾ, by it ﴿مَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا﴾ who understands what he is addressed with, and they are the believers ﴿وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ﴾ of punishment ﴿عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ and they are like the dead, not understanding what they are addressed with.

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا﴾ know; and the interrogative is for affirmation (taqrīr), and the wāw that enters upon it is for conjunction ﴿أَنَّا خَلَقْنَا لَهُمْ﴾ among people in general ﴿مِمَّا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِينَا﴾ i.e. which We made without partner or helper ﴿أَنْعَامًا﴾ they are camels, cattle and sheep ﴿فَهُمْ لَهَا مَالِكُونَ﴾ controlling

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿وَذَلَّلْنَاهَا﴾ We subjected them ﴿لَهُمْ فَمِنْهَا رَكُوبُهُمْ﴾ what they ride ﴿وَمِنْهَا يَأْكُلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ﴾ such as their wool, camel hair and goat hair ﴿وَمَشَارِبُ﴾ of their milk; plural of mashrab, in the sense of drinking or its place ﴿أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾ the One who blessed them with them, and so believe? i.e. they did not do that

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿وَاتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Allah ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ idols which they worship ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ be protected from the punishment of Allah the Exalted through the intercession of their gods, as they claim

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾ i.e. their gods; they are treated as beings endowed with reason ﴿نَصْرَهُمْ وَهُمْ﴾ their gods among the idols ﴿لَهُمْ جُنْدٌ﴾ for helping them, as they claim ﴿مُحْضَرُونَ﴾ in the Fire with them

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿فَلَا يَحْزُنْكَ قَوْلُهُمْ﴾ to you, "You are not one sent", and other than that ﴿إِنَّا نَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ﴾ of that and other things, and We will recompense them for it

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ know; and he is al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil ﴿أَنَّا خَلَقْنَاهُ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ﴾ semen, until We made him hardy and strong ﴿فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ﴾ intensely disputing with Us ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ making it plain, in denying the resurrection

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿وَضَرَبَ لَنَا مَثَلًا﴾ in that ﴿وَنَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ﴾ from semen, which is stranger than its like ﴿قَالَ مَنْ يُحْيِي الْعِظَامَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ﴾ i.e. decayed; and He did not say it with tāʾ [i.e. رَمِيمَةٌ] because it is a noun, not an adjective. It is narrated that he took a decayed bone, crumbled it, and said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Do you think Allah will bring this to life after it has rotted and decayed?" And he ﷺ said: "Yes, and He will put you into the Fire."

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿قُلْ يُحْيِيهَا الَّذِي أَنْشَأَهَا أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ خَلْقٍ﴾ created thing ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ in summary and in detail, before its creation and after its creation

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمْ﴾ among people in general ﴿مِنَ الشَّجَرِ الْأَخْضَرِ﴾ the markh and the ʿafār, or every tree except the jujube ﴿نَارًا فَإِذَا أَنْتُمْ مِنْهُ تُوقِدُونَ﴾ strike fire; and this indicates the power to resurrect, for He has combined in it water, fire and wood, and the water does not extinguish the fire, nor does the fire burn the wood

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿أَوَلَيْسَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ despite their immensity ﴿بِقَادِرٍ عَلَى أَنْ يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُمْ﴾ i.e. human beings, in smallness ﴿بَلَى وَهُوَ﴾ i.e. He is able to do that; He answered Himself ﴿الْخَلَّاقُ﴾ the One who creates much ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of everything

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا أَمْرُهُ﴾ His way ﴿إِذَا أَرَادَ شَيْئًا﴾ i.e. the creation of a thing ﴿أَنْ يَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾ i.e. and so it is; and in one reading in the accusative, conjoined to «يَقُولَ»

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿فَسُبْحَانَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ﴾ dominion; the wāw and the tāʾ were added for intensification (mubālagha), i.e. power over ﴿كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ you will be returned, in the Hereafter.
